sections.title: What does it mean?
sections.content: A Hungarian verb can contain information about who is doing the action. The verb ending can tell you whether the subject is I, you, or he/she.

sections.title: How does it work?
sections.content: Compare tanulok, tanulsz and tanul. The stem is tanul-. The ending changes with the person. First-person singular commonly has -ok/-ek/-ök, second-person singular commonly has -sz, and many third-person singular forms have no personal ending.

sections.title: Why does it look like this?
sections.content: English usually keeps the verb almost unchanged: I study, you study. Hungarian changes the verb more visibly. Because the verb carries this information, the pronoun can often be left out when the subject is clear.
When you meet a Hungarian verb, look at the ending before looking for a pronoun. The ending may already tell you who the subject is.
